organism: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Calsa (commercial bioethanol control strain)
medium: assay medium composition not yet retrieved from primary text - see Gaps G-01
assay: Cardinal Temperature Model with Inflection (CTMI) fitted by nonlinear regression (Quasi-Newton, Statistica 7.0); 3 independent replicates fitted independently
strain_background: Calsa, commercial bioethanol reference strain used as control
transfer_note: CTMI mu_max is the value AT T_opt in a broth/micro-growth format, not a 2-D agar colony-front rate. Never transfer to a filamentous mould.

organism: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Calsa (commercial bioethanol control strain)
assay: CTMI nonlinear fit; T_min defined by the source as the minimum temperature below which growth is not observed
quote: In this model, Tmin is the minimum temperature below which growth is not observed, Tmax is the maximum temperature above which growth ceases, and Topt corresponds to the optimal temperature at which μmax reaches its optimal value (μopt).
transfer_note: An extrapolated model parameter, NOT an observed no-growth point. Petra must not read sub-T_min as a death/inactivation rate.

organism: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Calsa (commercial bioethanol control strain)
transfer_note: T_opt of a thermotolerant bioethanol strain sits ABOVE Petra's 25/28/30 C panel. Not a species-generic yeast optimum.

organism: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Calsa (commercial bioethanol control strain)
transfer_note: Growth-cease boundary only. The source provides NO fitted mortality above T_max; Petra must not convert T_max into death.

organism: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Calsa (commercial bioethanol control strain)
parameter: CTMI fitted pH_min / pH_opt / pH_max (cardinal pH model, Rosso 1995)
assay: Cardinal pH Model (CPM) of Rosso et al. (1995) fitted by nonlinear regression
transfer_note: Secondary model to the temperature fit; Petra may use it only if pH is also a simulated field. Note CPM mu_max (0.19) differs from CTMI mu_max (0.21) because the two fits are separate regressions - do not reconcile silently.

medium: microtitre-plate growth assay medium; exact composition not retrieved - see Gaps G-02
assay: CTMI fitted to microtitre-plate growth data; SD from three independent non-linear fits
strain_background: CEN.PK113-7D, laboratory reference strain (NOT S288C; different lineage)
quote: Table 1. Estimated parameters with standard deviation from the CTMI fit for all the 13 strains. Standard deviations for each parameter were obtained from three independent non-linear fits. Strains / μopt (h−1) / Tmax (°C) / Tmin (°C) / Topt (°C) ... CEN.PK113-7D 0.368 ± 0.018 41.21 ± 0.81 3.08 ± 0.92 30.03 ± 0.85
transfer_note: CONFLICT WITH FUN-CTMI-001 kept deliberately: 0.368 vs 0.21 h^-1. Different strain (CEN.PK vs Calsa) and different assay; NOT averaged. CEN.PK113-7D is a different lineage from S288C - do not present as S288C.

medium: microtitre-plate growth assay; see Gaps G-02
assay: CTMI fit, three independent non-linear fits
uncertainty: T_min 3.08 ± 0.92; T_opt 30.03 ± 0.85; T_max 41.21 ± 0.81 °C. NOTE this table's column order is mu_opt, Tmax, Tmin, Topt - NOT ascending cardinal order.
transfer_note: T_opt 30.03 C matches Petra's 30 C panel exactly, so this is the better-matched cardinal set for a 25/28/30 C dish than the thermotolerant bioethanol strains. T_min ~3 C is far below FUN-CTMI-002's ~7.5 C: real between-strain/assay conflict, kept as two records.

organism: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ethanol Red (industrial bioethanol strain)
parameter: CTMI fitted mu_opt and T_opt (highest in this set)
medium: microtitre-plate growth assay; see Gaps G-02
assay: CTMI fit, three independent non-linear fits
transfer_note: Highest mu_opt in this sheet (0.467 h^-1, i.e. ln2/mu = 1.49 h doubling). Its T_opt is 35.26 C so this value is NOT attainable at Petra's 25-30 C panel; applying it at 30 C without the CTMI temperature factor would overestimate growth.

parameter: yield of biomass on glucose (Y biomass) at 30 C, ANAEROBIC
unit: mol biomass per mol glucose (as published; NO g/g conversion asserted)
medium: anaerobic glucose-limited chemostat, fixed dilution rate
assay: steady-state chemostat; calculated from specific net conversion rates (source Table 3), SE reported
quote: Table 5. Yields of biomass and main products on glucose of the three strains with their standard errors, calculated from the specific net conversion rates shown in Table 3. Y biomass (mol mol−1) Y CO2 (mol mol−1) Y ethanol (mol mol−1) Y glycerol (mol mol−1) ... CEN.PK113-7D ... 30 °C 0.498±0.011 1.717±0.033 1.636±0.032 0.144±0.003
transfer_note: ANAEROBIC glucose-limited chemostat. Petra's Y_x/glucose for an oxygen-exposed agar surface would be HIGHER; using this value on a surface is an explicit transfer that must be flagged. Units left exactly as published - Petra must not silently convert mol/mol to g/g without stating the biomass and glucose molar bases the authors used.

parameter: ethanol yield on glucose (Y ethanol) at 30 C - quantitative overflow/product relationship
uncertainty: 1.636 ± 0.032 mol mol^-1; theoretical maximum from 1 mol glucose is 2 mol ethanol, so this is 82% of the theoretical fermentative maximum
transfer_note: THIS is the documented yeast overflow/product stoichiometry Petra needs as the analogue of E. coli acetate overflow: at 30 C anaerobically, ~1.64 mol ethanol + 0.144 mol glycerol + 1.72 mol CO2 per mol glucose, with 0.498 mol/mol to biomass. Petra's E. coli overflow term must NOT be reused numerically.

parameter: glycerol yield on glucose (Y glycerol) at 30 C
transfer_note: Glycerol is the osmotic-relief by-product; it rises with temperature in ADY5/Ethanol Red but falls in CEN.PK (12 C 0.162 -> 39 C 0.113). Strain-dependent - do not pool.

organism: Saccharomyces cerevisiae ADY5 and Ethanol Red (industrial strains)
parameter: yield of biomass on glucose at 30 C, ANAEROBIC
medium: anaerobic glucose-limited chemostat, fixed dilution rate
assay: steady-state chemostat, calculated from specific net conversion rates
transfer_note: Y biomass varies 0.498-0.625 mol/mol between strains AT THE SAME temperature and same dilution rate - a 25% spread the source attributes to differing cellular ATP/energy demand, not to yield regulation. Petra must not treat Y_x/s as a species constant.
